I built the semantic layer in relay_dbt/models/semantic/. Both ./dbt parse and ./mf validate-configs pass. Test queries return sensible numbers: June 2025 shows MRR of $4.15M across 1,185 paying customers. Customer counts reconcile month by month (starting + new + reactivated − churned = ending).

Helper models (8 SQL tables, built with ./dbt build):
- sem_subscription_months and sem_customer_months: month-end MRR per subscription, and each account's paying / new / reactivated / churned status per month.
- sem_invoices, sem_revenue_recognition, sem_payments, sem_credit_notes, sem_usage_daily, sem_opportunities: cleaned copies of the existing mart tables with the rules below applied.

Semantic models:
- Dimension tables: accounts (segment, region, country, billing currency, parent account, deleted/internal flags), plans (plan name, family, billing interval), sales_reps (team, region, rep name) and fiscal_calendar (fiscal year runs Feb–Jan and is named for the year it ends).
- Fact tables: subscription_months, customer_months, invoices, revenue_recognition, payments, credit_notes, usage_daily, opportunities.

Metrics:
- Recurring revenue and customers: mrr, arr, mrr_local_currency, paid_seats, active_subscriptions, paying_customers, arpa, new_customers, reactivated_customers, churned_customers, customers_at_start_of_month, logo_churn_rate.
- Finance: billings, billings_incl_tax, invoice_count, recognized_revenue, cash_collected, refunds, refund_count, net_cash_collected, billable_usage, accounts_with_usage.
- Sales: bookings, new_bookings, expansion_bookings, open_pipeline, won_deals, lost_deals, closed_deals, win_rate.

Business rules I took from the data:
- Internal accounts excluded: the 60 Relay QA/test accounts are left out of every metric. Deleted accounts stay in, so history doesn't change when an account is deleted.
- MRR and paying customers: only subscriptions whose status is active on the last day of the month count. MRR is seats × contracted price × (1 − discount), with annual plans divided by 12, excluding tax, converted to USD at the month-end rate. Trials, past-due and cancelled subscriptions are excluded.
- Monthly grain: MRR, customer counts and recognized revenue go down to month, not day. At quarter or year level, MRR and customer counts show the last month-end.
- New vs. reactivated: "new" means an account's first-ever paying month. An account that comes back after churning is counted as reactivated, not new.
- Churn: an account that was paying last month-end and isn't now. logo_churn_rate is churned ÷ customers at the start of the month; at quarter or year level it's the average monthly rate, not cumulative churn.
- Customer unit: customers are counted per account. Subsidiaries count separately from their parent.
- Billings and revenue: billings are open, paid and uncollectible invoices, net of discount and excluding tax; drafts and voids are left out. Recognized revenue uses the same invoices, spread daily over each subscription's service period, with services invoices recognized when issued. It is not reduced by refunds.
- Cash and refunds: cash collected counts successful payments only, including tax. "Refunds" are the credit notes, since there are no negative payments in the data.
- Billable usage: API calls only. Health checks are left out because they're a constant 288 automated pings per account per day.
- Sales: bookings are won deal value (annual contract value in USD) by close date; new bookings are won deals of type 'new'. Win rate is won ÷ (won + lost) by deal count, ignoring open deals.

Judgement calls you may want to review:
- Past-due subscriptions are excluded from MRR, because in this data they always follow an uncollectible invoice. If you want to count them until they're cancelled, as Stripe does, the filter is in sem_subscription_months.sql.
- Customers are counted per account, not rolled up to the parent account.
- Billable usage includes calls made during free trials, which are about 3% of the total.

Built comprehensive dbt semantic layer for Relay's SaaS metrics with 9 semantic models (subscriptions, invoices, payments, revenue_recognition, credit_notes, opportunities, usage, accounts, plans, sales_reps) and 19 metrics (MRR, ARR, paying customers, ARPA, billings, recognized revenue, cash collected, refunds, bookings, win rate, churn, usage) covering all finance and sales dimensions (segment, region, currency, plan, sales team). All models have explicit descriptions of what they include/exclude. Both dbt parse and mf validate-configs pass successfully.

The semantic layer is in `relay_dbt/models/semantic/`; `./dbt parse` and `./mf validate-configs` both pass (0 errors, 1 warning, explained below). Helper models build with all 23 data tests passing, and sample queries by month, fiscal quarter, segment, region, plan family and sales team return sensible numbers.

## What I defined

- **12 semantic models:** `customers`, `accounts`, `plans`, `sales_reps`, `subscription_months`, `customer_months`, `invoices`, `revenue_schedule`, `payments`, `credit_notes`, `usage_daily`, `opportunities`.
- **36 metrics**, all in USD, each with a description of what it includes and excludes:
  - Recurring: `mrr`, `arr`, `paying_customers`, `arpa`, `paying_subscriptions`, `trialing_subscriptions`, `paying_seats`
  - Lifecycle: `new_customers`, `reactivated_customers`, `churned_customers`, `customers_at_period_start`, `logo_churn_rate`
  - Billing and cash: `billings`, `subscription_billings`, `services_billings`, `tax_billed`, `invoices_billed`, `recognized_revenue`, `cash_collected`, `refunds`, `refund_count`, `net_cash_collected`, `payment_attempts`, `failed_payments`, `payment_failure_rate`
  - Usage: `billable_usage`, `total_usage`, `accounts_with_billable_usage`
  - Sales: `bookings`, `new_bookings`, `expansion_bookings`, `won_opportunities`, `lost_opportunities`, `closed_opportunities`, `win_rate`, `open_pipeline`
- **Dimensions:** customer and account segment, region, country and billing currency; plan name, plan family and billing interval; sales rep, team and rep region; transaction currency; invoice type and status; payment method and status; refund reason; usage event type; opportunity type and stage.
- **Time grains:** calendar grains plus `fiscal_quarter` and `fiscal_year` (the fiscal year starts 1 February).
- **11 helper SQL tables** (`sem_*`, schema `semantic`) that do the USD conversion, account filtering and customer roll-up.

## Business logic I worked out from the data

- **Internal accounts are excluded everywhere.** The "Relay QA / Demo / Sandbox" accounts carry about 10% of invoice value and about 23% of API calls.
- **Currency:** amounts are in minor units, and JPY has none, so each is scaled by its currency's exponent and converted at the FX rate of the relevant date.
- **MRR:** seats × unit price × (1 − discount), with annual plans divided by 12. It is a month-end balance, so a quarter or year shows the last month-end rather than a sum.
- **Customers are logos.** The 65 child accounts roll up to their parent, so `customer__segment` and `customer__region` are the parent's; `account__segment` and `account__region` give the billed account's own values.
- **New vs churned:** new customers are first-ever paying; win-backs are counted separately as reactivated. Churn is paying at the previous month-end and not at this one, divided by customers at the start of the period.
- **Billings and recognized revenue** are net of discounts, exclude tax, and exclude draft and void invoices.
- **Cash collected** counts succeeded payments only (565 failed attempts are excluded) and includes tax.
- **Billable usage** is `api_call` only; `health_check` is a constant 288 per account per day, which looks like monitoring pings.
- **Bookings** are closed-won amounts by close date; win rate is won ÷ (won + lost) by count, with open opportunities excluded.

## Judgement calls to confirm

- **Soft-deleted accounts are excluded entirely** (45 accounts). They had active subscriptions before deletion but no invoices or opportunities at all, so I treated them as non-customers. If they were real customers, historical MRR and churn are understated.
- **`past_due` counts as paying** (in MRR and paying customers); only trialing and canceled are excluded.
- **Uncollectible invoices stay in billings and recognized revenue**, treated as bad debt rather than reversed revenue.
- **Refunds are credit notes**, all four reasons. There is no refund record in payments, and neither billings nor recognized revenue is reduced by them.

## Known limits

- **Time spine warning:** `validate-configs` warns that two day-grain time spines exist. The project's own spine is outside the kept folder, so I added a second one to carry the fiscal grains. Both cover the same dates, so results are the same whichever is used; moving the fiscal columns onto the original spine would clear the warning.
- **Month-grain metrics at day grain:** MRR, lifecycle metrics and recognized revenue are dated on the last day of the month, so they should be queried by month or coarser.
- **Recognized revenue after June 2025** is revenue already scheduled from issued invoices, not a forecast.
- **No local-currency metrics:** every amount is USD; currency is available only as a slicing dimension.

Built the Relay semantic layer in relay_dbt/models/semantic/. `./dbt parse` and `./mf validate-configs` both pass, and sample queries by quarter, year and segment gave plausible values (not reconciled to source figures). Helper models (sem_accounts, sem_customer_months, sem_invoices, sem_revenue, sem_payments, sem_credit_notes, sem_usage) exclude internal accounts, roll child accounts up to their parent customer, and convert amounts to USD. Semantic models: accounts, sales_reps, customer_months, invoices, revenue_recognition, payments, credit_notes, usage, opportunities. Metrics: mrr, arr, paying_customers, arpa, new_customers, logo_churn, opening_customers, churn_rate, billings, recognized_revenue, cash_collected, refunds, billable_usage, bookings, new_bookings, won_opportunities, closed_opportunities, win_rate, new_business_win_rate. Dimensions: segment, region, country, plan, plan family, billing interval, currency, invoice type and status, payment method, refund reason, opportunity type and stage, sales rep, team and rep region. Every model, dimension, measure and metric has a description stating inclusions and exclusions. Key rules: MRR counts active and past_due subscriptions only (annual plans ÷12, month-end FX); month-end metrics are snapshots, not summed across months; billings exclude draft and void invoices and tax; revenue is recognized straight-line over the service period, with future months dropped; cash counts succeeded payments only; usage counts api_call only; win rate is won ÷ (won+lost). Limitation: the 30 customers with subscriptions in more than one currency have customer counts attributed to their largest-MRR subscription's plan and currency; MRR itself is exact by plan.
